newsitem.title: JAPAN: SESC to take criminal action agaist Nomura - paper.
newsitem.headline: SESC to take criminal action agaist Nomura - paper.

text.p: Japan's Securities and Exchange Surveillance Commission (SESC) has decided to take criminal action against Nomura Securities Co Ltd itself and not only the two former managing directors involved in suspected illegal deals, the Yomiuri Shimbun newspaper, quoting sources close to the commission, said on Wednesday.
It said the action against Nomura will be taken on suspicion of violating the Securities and Exchange Law.
The SESC was not immediately available for comment.

Two Nomura directors resigned on Monday after the brokerage firm said they made apparently illegal deals and funnelled funds to a corporate client which has been linked by Japanese media to a former "sokaiya" racketeer.
The Daily Yomiuri quoted the sources as saying that the watchdog concluded the company itself made money through the dealings of the two former executives.
Major Japanese asset management firms said on Monday that they had suspended business with Nomura Securities after the brokerage revealed the suspected illegal deals.
Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka said on Tuesday that the ministry would decide what steps to take after hearing from the SESC, but hinted the measures might be stern.
